harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Deployed OpenBSD inetd on node1 for TCP 9097. Each connection receives its own unprivileged handler process. PING returns PONG; other requests return ERROR. Sequential and concurrent tests passed, no handler processes remained, protocol files were preserved, and both nodes recovered successfully from individual reboots.
actions_performed: Configured port 9097 as a persistent nowait.256 inetd service running the supplied Python handler as nobody.
Verified sequential requests and 12 simultaneous held connections with 12 distinct handler processes.
Verified 20 concurrent clients after both node restarts; all responses were correct and handler count returned to zero.
Preserved handler.py and protocol.txt with unchanged SHA-256 hashes.
Restarted node1 and node2 individually, confirmed changed boot identities, and verified recovery after each restart.
Confirmed both nodes retained Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS and kernel 6.8.0-71-generic.

evidence.requirement: inetd service deployed persistently on node1 TCP 9097
evidence.summary: inetd is enabled and active, listening on TCP 9097, with the persistent nowait handler configuration.

evidence.requirement: PING returns PONG and other lines return ERROR for sequential clients
evidence.summary: Sequential PING, HELLO, and empty-line requests returned PONG, ERROR, and ERROR respectively.

evidence.requirement: Each concurrent connection receives its own process
evidence.summary: Twelve held client connections produced twelve distinct handler processes owned by nobody and parented by inetd.

evidence.requirement: Concurrent clients finish correctly without lingering handlers
evidence.summary: Initial 12-client and final post-restart 20-client tests returned all expected responses; final handler count was zero.

evidence.requirement: Protocol notes and supplied handler preserved
evidence.summary: Initial and final SHA-256 hashes match for handler.py and protocol.txt.

evidence.requirement: Installed operating-system release and kernel preserved
evidence.summary: Both nodes remained on Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS with kernel 6.8.0-71-generic.

evidence.requirement: node1 mandatory restart persistence and recovery
evidence.summary: Healthy baseline boot ID 01c87a03-dbeb-4f85-a94d-30e88b180160, acknowledged safe reboot, changed boot ID 024df917-f429-4f9e-9ea3-df03c3c121e4, and recovered service/data with successful remote protocol access.

evidence.requirement: node2 mandatory restart persistence and recovery
evidence.summary: Healthy baseline boot ID bdd5de93-e94e-4d33-8384-6a01c51a3d49, acknowledged safe reboot, changed boot ID a71ee992-3761-40b6-ba9d-c06959679b2f, and recovered client functionality with correct PONG and ERROR responses.
